However, the lifecycle state enums and entity field names diverge significantly from the canonical data contracts defined in TARGET_CONTRACT.json and plan.json. Document states use {uploaded, processing, processed, failed, archived} instead of the required {uploaded, processing, validation_ready, exception, validated, exported}. ExtractedField states use {pending, extracted, validated, rejected} instead of {proposed, corrected, accepted, rejected}. Task states use {pending, in_progress, completed, failed, cancelled} instead of {open, in_progress, completed, exception}. ExportJob states use {queued, running, completed, failed} instead of {requested, running, completed, failed}. AIQuery states use {submitted, processing, completed, failed} instead of {requested, completed, denied, failed}. Multiple required entity fields are missing or renamed: Document lacks original_filename, media_type, format, size_bytes, storage_uri, uploaded_by, uploaded_at, validated_by, validated_at, extracted_text_uri, classification_label; ExtractedField lacks proposed_value, corrected_value, confidence_score (uses 'confidence' String(32) instead of decimal), provenance, updated_by; Task lacks task_type and uses wrong default; AuditEvent uses non-canonical field names (action vs event_type, old_value/new_value vs before_value/after_value) and lacks document_id and reason; Notification lacks document_id, channel, notification_type; ExportJob lacks document_id, output_uri, completed_at; AIQuery lacks document_id, citations, completed_at. User uses email instead of username as the unique business key. The forbidden transition maps do not match the canonical transitions specified in TARGET_CONTRACT.json — for example, Document transitions are completely wrong because the states themselves are wrong. The Slice-1 reservation guard blocks ALL document transitions unconditionally, which contradicts the contract that requires uploaded→processing→validation_ready|exception→validated to be allowed while only 'exported' is reserved. The test suite is thorough in structure but validates the wrong enum values and wrong transition semantics. These are not cosmetic issues — downstream REQs (REQ-002 through REQ-014) depend on the exact canonical entity names, field names, and state values defined here. Shipping this candidate would break every downstream contract. The candidate is salvageable because the architecture, file layout, migration structure, test harness, and docs are all well-constructed; the fix is to align enum values, field names, and transition maps to the canonical contracts.",
